segments.text: Hey friends, just give me the next 15
minutes and I promise you this—if you truly understand and apply what I’m
going to share in today’s video, then 2026 will become the best year of your life.
It will be the breakthrough year you’ve
been searching for over the past many years.
How will that happen?
Because today I’m not going to give you just motivational talk.
Today, with the help of a book that is 120 years old—a true classic—I’m
going to share ideas that can help you reprogram your mind.
While many people are getting brainwashed in the name of success, wasting
their time, losing their money, and getting caught up in the wrong things, I
will teach you how to reprogram yourself for success—by focusing on just one thing.
What is that one thing?
Today, I’ll explain it to you through a story.
And within that single story are seven amazing lessons from this book.
If you truly understand these seven lessons, you’ll learn how to reprogram
yourself not just at a conscious level, but at a subconscious level.
You’ll create a kind of inner programming that naturally takes you toward success.
In 2026, as always, I’ll share one powerful lesson with you
in a story format so that these ideas stay with you for a long time.
Now, let’s start.
There was a boy named Arjun who had no one in the world.
For certain reasons, he decided to go and live in the forest.
So he went deep into the jungle, where there were lush green trees all around.
There were many mountains, with caves inside them.
Many times, he would go and live in those caves.
Arjun was not very intelligent, nor was he very powerful, but he had something
truly special—that was discipline, a strong mind, and a powerful character.
His character was such that everyone liked him.
There were no humans
in the forest, but many animals had become Arjun’s friends. Why?
Because Arjun had helped those animals many times.
If a deer’s fawn fell sick, he would take care of it.
Sometimes he helped elephants find water.
In this way, he built friendships with different animals.
Many times, the thought crossed his mind, “These animals could eat me.
They could hurt me.” But he believed in one thing—that whatever his thinking
is like, the same kind of things will happen to him.
That’s why every morning he reminded himself that all the animals in the jungle
were his friends, and that if he helped them, someday they would help him too.
And because of this way of thinking, while most animals saw
humans as enemies, they began to see Arjun as a friend.
This is how his life was going on.
Then one morning, Arjun
decided to move away from the place where he was living and go somewhere else.
Because he felt like eating mangoes, and a bird had told him that a few
kilometers away from where he lived, there were many mango trees loaded
with delicious mangoes.
So that day, he decided that instead of eating leaves and roots, he would
eat fruit.
Just to get that, he set out on a journey.
After walking for a long time, he finally found a mango tree.
He went there, ate mangoes, and collected many to carry with him.
But as he was returning toward his home, his foot slipped at one point,
and all the mangoes he had with him fell into the river.
They were all washed away by the flowing water.
Somehow, he manages to save himself, but not a single mango is left.
All the mangoes are swept away by the river.
Now negativity starts creeping into his mind—“Why does this always happen to me?
I walked so far and worked so hard to collect these mangoes.
Now I won’t have any mangoes left.”
“Now I’ll have to eat the same food again.” But after feeling disappointed
for a while, he admits to himself, “No, this is my mistake.
If I had walked more carefully, maybe I wouldn’t have slipped.” Instead of blaming
anything or anyone, he regains control over himself
and goes back to the cave near which he often spent his nights.
But when he reaches the
cave that day, he feels something strange the moment he gets there.
It’s as if his sixth sense gets activated.
His breathing almost stops, and his chest feels heavy.
He realizes that there is something inside the cave—something dangerous.
So, gathering his courage, he shouts and asks, “Who is inside?”
For some time, there is no sound at all.
Then, after a while, a terrifying voice comes from inside, saying, “I am the one
who can bring elephants to their knees, who can even break the bones of a
rhinoceros.” The voice is so frightening that Arjun’s breath catches in his throat.
His hands and feet start sweating, and his heartbeat begins to race.
Because of the mangoes he had eaten, his stomach starts acting up.
He feels such weakness throughout his body that he can’t even take a
single step forward.
Fear completely consumes him.
Just then, a wolf passes by.
This wolf knows Arjun, so it comes up to him and asks, “Arjun, what happened?”
Arjun tells him that there is something inside the cave—something terrifying
and dangerous—and that he doesn’t have the courage to go inside.
The wolf says confidently, “What’s there to be afraid of?
I’ll go.
I’ll check what it is, who it is.” The wolf goes near the cave and
calls out, “Who is there?
Come out!” Just then, the same terrifying voice comes from
inside again and says, “I am the one who kills and eats wolves.
I love their flesh.
I am the one who can kill all animals.” The voice is
as loud and thunderous, like a lightning strike.
The wolf also becomes scared.
He starts thinking, “What if there’s a lion inside?
Lions and wolves have been enemies for a long time.” Anyway, Arjun
wasn’t his favorite either—yes, he liked other wolves much more.
And since he didn’t like Arjun
that much, he decided he wouldn’t risk his life for him.
The wolf gets scared and says, “Don’t worry.
I know an animal who has never lost a single battle till date.”
“I’ll call him and bring him here.”
The wolf goes and brings the lion.
A lion whose
list of achievements was very long—one who had never lost to any animal.
The wolf tells him everything, and the lion says, “Don’t worry, I’ll handle
it.” The lion goes to the front of the cave and roars loudly.
In response, a spine‑chilling voice comes back, “Lion, come on in.
I’ve been waiting for you for
a long time.” Today, I’ll show you what it feels like to lose.
Normally, the lion had never been defeated,
but hearing that voice from inside makes him doubt himself somewhere.
He also becomes scared, thinking, “What if I lose today?
Or what if there’s an elephant inside?
It would be very difficult for me to defeat it.”
My reputation could be ruined,” so he doesn’t take the risk either.
But then he says, “Don’t worry.
I’ll call a few of my friends.
Even if there is an elephant inside, they’ll definitely defeat it.”
After that, the lion goes.
He has two friends—an elephant and a rhinoceros—whom
he has never been able to defeat, so he had befriended them.
He calls them over; both are very experienced.
When they come, even to fight the biggest animals, they make their presence
known with a loud call. They ask, “Who is inside?
Come out!” Once again, a spine‑chilling voice comes from inside, saying, “I
am the one who hunts elephants.
I am the one who kills rhinoceroses and cuts off
their horns.” Now even these two animals grow tense.
A picture starts
forming in their minds—maybe inside there isn’t just an animal or even a
human, but someone with immense power, or with weapons that could kill them.
Different thoughts start running through their minds.
Images begin to form because
they had often seen how humans had killed rhinos, and even other humans.
This frightening vision shakes them to the core.
After that, all of them become exhausted.
No one has the courage to go into the cave.
Just then, a frog standing far away, who has been watching all
of this, comes forward.
The frog tells everyone, “Wait, I’ll check who it is.” All the
animals—and even Arjun—are a little shocked, wondering what the frog will do.
But the frog is completely calm.
Then he goes right up to the cave.
Look friends, if you’ve been following the story carefully, you’ll notice that one
thing came into the minds of all these animals—a single thing
that, many times, defeated even the strongest creatures in the jungle.
What was that thing?
That thing was thoughts, or thinking.
And this is exactly what the book explains in detail—how your own
thoughts can defeat you even before you actually face a challenge.
Whether something actually exists or not, your thoughts create fear in your
life, stopping you from taking the actions you need to take.
And this is exactly what I want to explain to you through this story.
I’ve already shared
six things with you through this story, which I will explain further.
Your thoughts impact all six of these things.
Actually, there are seven things that the frog will reveal later.
But if you want to learn about this—how to work on your thoughts,
how to reprogram yourself—this is explained in the book.

When it feels like all hope is lost, and there’s
no one left to call for help, that’s when a frog appears.
The frog is very small, but its calmness is immense.
This frog doesn’t go into imagination or panic mode at all.
It goes straight to the front and says, “Whatever is out
there, come face me.” Then, again, that terrifying voice comes.
But this frog does not get scared.
No negative thoughts enter its mind.
It simply says once more, “Come out, or we will all come in and won’t let you
go.” Now, as soon as the frog says this, the voice inside hesitates a little.
Slowly, something emerges from inside, and its shadow looks huge.
But when it comes out, everyone sees it—it’s a mouse, a small, dirty mouse.
The thing is, the mouse’s voice sounds so loud because
the cave is shaped in a way that echoes every sound.
It was very dark, and because it was so dark, nothing could be clearly seen.
After seeing the mouse, everyone realizes
that there was no dangerous animal at all—it was just a mouse.
And what was truly the most dangerous thing were their thoughts.
The mouse feels very embarrassed and explains
that since the weather outside was bad, it had come into the cave to hide.
But when it saw Arjun, it got scared and thought, “Maybe this
human will kill me or eat me,” so it did all of this.
The mouse apologizes and begs for its life.
Then Arjun laughs and says to it, “I’m your friend—I
don’t eat animals.” And that’s when everyone realizes the truth.
All the beings there were seeing each other as enemies.
But in reality, they had only one true enemy—their own thoughts.
My question is, friends, in 2026, what is that one
voice inside you—the one coming from your own “cave”—that’s scaring you?
Maybe it’s stopping you from starting a
new business, or creating content, or taking some other action.
You may need to close a new
client, but there’s a voice inside you that keeps saying, “You can’t do it.
You don’t have what it takes.
You don’t have the resources.” Remember, all of these things are nothing but
your thoughts.
And these thoughts—until they remain negative—your
chances of creating positive outcomes in life will be very limited.
So, if you truly want to brainwash yourself in 2026, just like
I did to achieve my own success, then work on your thoughts.
Start bringing in as many positive thoughts as possible.
And having positive thoughts doesn’t mean becoming a blind optimist—no.
Positive thoughts mean that even
in the worst situations, you can act well, make progress, and grow.
Your thoughts create everything in your life.
This book has seven chapters.
It explains how your thoughts shape your character—whether good or bad.
Just like Arjun’s character
was good, all the animals in the jungle became his friends.
Secondly, your thoughts also create
your circumstances—like when Arjun’s mangoes fell.
He was sad.
Then he made his thoughts positive, and instead of staying
by the river or spending time there, he moved toward the cave.
Third, when negative thoughts came to Arjun, they also affected
his health—he started sweating, and his stomach acted up.
Fourth, the wolf had thoughts too.
Many times, your thoughts determine your purpose.
The wolf didn’t risk his life because he didn’t have a strong purpose.
He didn’t have strong thoughts.
He didn’t want to risk his life for Arjun.
Fifth, your thoughts can also shake your achievements.
The lion had many achievements, but
the thought came that his achievements could be ruined, so he didn’t take action.
Sixth, your thoughts are often aligned with your vision.
If the visions or ideas coming to your mind are negative—just like they came
to the elephant and the rhino—then you won’t be able to take positive actions.
And seventh, the serenity and
calmness of the frog—its thoughts were neither overly positive nor negative.
The frog had a calmness inside, and it was its thoughts that gave it that calmness.
These seven lessons are explained very well in the book.
